options: Although he studied a lot, he failed the exam
He not only studied but also passed
He studied together with a friend and failed
items.explanation: Beraber after -mAklA is a concession: “although.” “Together” would come with a noun.

items.prompt: Kitabı okumakla kalmadı, filmini de izledi.
options: He not only read the book but also watched the movie
Although he read the book, he didn't watch the movie
items.say: Kitabı okumakla kalmadı, filmini de izledi.
items.explanation: Kalmadı + da is the second floor: he also watched the movie.

options: Although he said hello, he left
items.explanation: Yetinmek means “to settle for”: he said hello, and that's it.
-mAklA hata etmek is “to make a mistake by…,” in other words “you shouldn't have.”

options: The director was accused of a meeting
The director only organized the meeting
The director is in charge of organizing the meeting
items.explanation: -mAklA görevli is “to be in charge of…”

exercises.instruction: Match the construction and the meaning

items.explanation: All these words ask “with what?” — so the verb comes to them in the -mAklA form.

items.translation: Although he was right, he behaved rudely.
items.explanation: You need the -mAk noun + -lA: ol-mak-la beraber.

items.translation: He not only said it but also did it.
items.explanation: The second part has da, so the first one didn't stop there: kalmadı.

items.translation: He didn't talk, he just smiled.
items.explanation: He settled for a smile: yetindi.

items.translation: Right now I'm busy looking for an apartment.
items.explanation: “Busy with what?” — -mAklA meşgul.
“Accuse of what?” — -mAklA suçlamak.

items.translation: Although he was sick, he went to work.
items.explanation: Concession: hasta olmakla birlikte, “although he was sick.”

items.translation: He not only listened but also took notes.
items.say: Sadece dinlemekle kalmadı, not da aldı.
items.explanation: You need -mAk + -lA: dinle-mek-le. The second part takes da.
-mAklA iyi etmek is “to do well to…”
Meşgul asks “with what?” — oynamakla.

exercises.instruction: Contract with the realtor: stamp the blank
exercises.description: A contract clause with a blank; the learner applies one of four stamps (beraber, kalma-, yetin-, suçla-; keys 1–4), and the stamp is printed into the text. Logic is in index.html.

items.s: Daire deniz manzaralı olmakla ___ biraz küçük.
items.ru: The apartment has a sea view, although it's a bit small.
items.explanation: They admitted a plus and objected right away. That's a concession: beraber.

items.s: Emlakçı sadece anahtarı vermekle ___, eşyaları da taşıdı.
items.ru: The realtor not only handed over the key but also carried the stuff.
items.explanation: The second part has da, so the first action wasn't the last: kalmadı.

items.ru: Haggling didn't work out — we just said thanks.
items.explanation: We just said thanks, and that's it: yetindik.

items.ru: The neighbor accused us of making noise.
items.explanation: “Accuse of what?” — suçladı.

items.s: Fiyatı yüksek olmakla ___ herkes almak istiyor.
items.ru: Although the price is high, everyone wants to buy.
items.explanation: The price is high, but everyone wants it. Concession: beraber.

items.s: Sadece fotoğraf çekmekle ___, sahilde yürüdük de.
items.ru: We not only took photos but also walked along the beach.
items.explanation: The second action has de, so kalmadık.

items.ru: The realtor was accused of cheating clients.
items.explanation: He was accused, so it's passive: suçlandı.

items.ru: We just looked at the apartment, didn't buy.
items.explanation: We looked and settled for that: yetindik.

options: Although he knew, he didn't say
He not only knew but also said
items.explanation: Beraber after -mAklA means “although.”

items.statement: After -mAklA kalmadı, the second part usually has da/de.
items.explanation: Yes. The second floor stands on da/de or bile.

options: You came, but you shouldn't have
items.explanation: -mAklA iyi etmek is “to do well to…”

items.statement: Annemle beraber and okumakla beraber are the same construction.
items.explanation: No. With a noun it's “together with,” with a -mAk verb it's “although.”

items.prompt: “He was accused of lying” in Turkish:
items.explanation: “Accuse of what?” — -mAklA suçlamak, here passive: suçlandı.
